title: A Solutions Manual for Theory of Finite Automata
excerpt: I proposed an automata theory textbook to John Carroll when I was an undergraduate. The book now has a restored edition and a new solutions manual.

title: Dr. Witold Litwin
excerpt: Witold Litwin’s pioneering work on linear hashing, multidatabase systems, scalable distributed data structures, and many other fields—and the friendship that grew from it.

title: Delta Compression
excerpt: Encoding a file as its differences from an earlier version, in linear time, and rebuilding it in the space the old version occupies.

title: No Perfect Guardrail
excerpt: The mathematical limits of LLM guardrails, the risks of letting models act, and the people who must answer when safeguards fail.

title: Why Pentexoire
excerpt: A search for a one-word domain name led to Pentexoire, a part of the kingdom of Prester John in the Travels of Sir John Mandeville.

title: On Fathers
excerpt: A photocopied list I first read as a teenager, tracing how a child's estimate of a father changes over a lifetime.

title: Ceph and the SSRC
excerpt: Ceph’s origins in the SSRC, the earlier work on Swift and RAMA, and Dr. Sage Weil’s research and development of the file system.

title: Retiring with Dr. Ethan Miller
excerpt: Retiring from UC Santa Cruz with my closest colleague and friend, after decades of building the SSRC and CRSS together.

title: The Darrell and Elaine Long Professorship in Experimental Physics
excerpt: Why Elaine and I endowed a professorship in experimental physics at UC Santa Cruz, and the work of its first holder, Dr. Bruce Schumm.

excerpt: A Rust library for studying threshold sharing, ramp schemes, general access structures, visual cryptography, and share verification.

title: Random Number Generators in Rust
excerpt: The entropy library provides PRNGs and CSPRNGs, exact integer sampling, continuous distributions, reproducible parallel streams, and statistical tests.

title: On Time
excerpt: The only thing you truly possess is time. Money is what other people give you in exchange for your time.

title: Performance Evaluation: Do It Right or Don't Do It
excerpt: Bad performance evaluation is endemic in systems research. We have the methods and tools to do it correctly.

title: Ercole Bottani (1897–1978)

title: Luigi Dadda (1923–2012)
excerpt: Dadda helped establish computing in Italy and developed the multiplier that bears his name during a long career at the Politecnico di Milano.

title: Domenico Ferrari
excerpt: My academic grandfather's work on performance evaluation, Berkeley Unix, and network quality of service.

title: Angelo Barbagelata (1875–1960)
excerpt: Barbagelata's career in electrical measurement, engineering practice, and teaching at the Politecnico di Milano.

title: Dr. Jehan-François Pâris
excerpt: My doctoral advisor at UC San Diego, the Gemini replicated file system, and a collaboration spanning nearly four decades and sixty-nine publications.
